objectives.statement: Calculate storage capacity
Perform rigging and load calculations
Calculate flow rates (e.g., ventilation, hydraulic, pneumatic)
Calculate slope angle and depth ratio for trenching and excavation
Calculate noise hazards (e.g., Time-Weighted Average [TWA], dual machinery, noise reduction rates)
Calculate climate and environmental conditions (e.g., ambient temperature, wind chill, heat index)
Calculate fall protection parameters (e.g., free-fall distance, maximum arresting force, force of impact, total fall distance, clearance)
Calculate lagging indicators (e.g., incidence rates, lost time, direct costs of incidents)
Calculate manual lift parameters (i.e., NIOSH lifting equation)
Perform general physics calculations (e.g., force, acceleration, velocity, momentum, friction)
Calculate descriptive statistics (e.g., central tendency, variability, probability, standard deviation)
Calculate probability of failure mode
Calculate financial indicators (e.g., cost-benefit analysis, cost of risk, life cycle cost, return on investment, effects of losses)
Conduct exposure assessments (e.g., biological, chemical, Threshold Limit Value [TLV], Short-Term Exposure Limits [STEL], Time-Weighted Average [TWA])
Calculate radiation exposure (e.g., shielding, half-life, dosage)
Perform unit conversions (e.g., metric/imperial units)
Understand safety management systems for development of programs (e.g., ISO 45001, ANSI Z10.0)
Apply the hierarchy of hazard controls
Apply appropriate hazard and risk analysis methods (e.g., hazard analysis, failure modes and effects analysis, fault tree analysis, fishbone, what-if and checklist analysis, change analysis)
Apply risk matrix methodology for ranking and mitigation of risks
Implement the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS)
Implement hazardous energy control programs (e.g., electrical, hydraulic, thermal, kinetic, mechanical, magnetic)
Understand general electrical principles (e.g., Ohm’s Law, power, impedance, energy, resistance, circuits)
Understand the key safety fundamentals of:
Trenching and excavations
Working at heights
Slips, trips, and falls
Machine guarding
Powered industrial trucks
Hoisting and rigging
Scaffolding
Process safety
Confined spaces
Fleet and driver safety
Personal protective equipment (PPE)
Compressed gasses/pressure vessels
Facilitate incident investigations (e.g., root causes, contributing factors, data collection, analysis, chain of custody, high risk incidents)
Understand key concepts regarding management of change
Interpret leading and lagging indicators
Have awareness of emerging technologies (e.g., data mining, robotics, drones, artificial intelligence)
Understand elements of an ergonomics program
Identify ergonomic risk factors
Repetition
Force
Awkward/static postures
Other stressors (e.g., contact, vibration, lighting, temperature conditions)
Define work-related musculoskeletal ergonomic injuries
Apply ergonomic principles for workspace design (e.g., in-office, remote, field, assembly station, bench/hood)
Apply ergonomic principles to manual material handling (e.g., safe lifting)
Identify ergonomic work practice controls (e.g., exoskeleton, job rotation, early symptom intervention)
Identify ergonomic qualitative and quantitative analysis methods (e.g., NIOSH Lifting Equation, anthropometry, Rapid Entire Body Assessment [REBA], Rapid Upper Limb Assessment [RULA])
Understand the fundamentals of fire science (e.g., classification, fire pentagon/tetrahedron, upper and lower explosive/flammable limits)
Understand flammable and combustible materials (e.g., chemical and physical properties, handling, compatibility)
Understand electrical hazards and applicable hazard controls:
Electrostatic discharge
Overcurrent protection
Arc flash
Ground fault circuit interrupter
Grounding and bonding
Hazardous area classifications (e.g., NFPA classifications, non-intrinsically safe)
Understand hazards during hot work operations
Identify combustible dust hazards (e.g., conflagration, sources of ignition)
Understand fire detection systems
Understand fire suppression systems
Identify fire extinguisher types, use, and requirements
Understand segregation and separation (e.g., flammable materials storage and ventilation)
Apply effective housekeeping practices (e.g., dust control, disposal of combustibles)
Select appropriate fire prevention signs and labels
Understand the elements of an emergency response plan
Identify the risks associated with the following sources of emergencies and disasters:
Natural
Human
Biological (e.g., pandemic, bioterrorism)
Understand the key elements of preparing for an emergency (e.g., drills, worksite security, evacuation routes, life safety, medical/first aid)
Identify the elements of disaster response and recovery (e.g., incident command, business continuity)
Identify the key elements of a workplace violence prevention program
Understand safety considerations for lone workers
Understand fundamental requirements of industrial hygiene programs (e.g., hearing conservation, respiratory protection, medical surveillance)
Understand general chemistry concepts (e.g., classification, composition, nomenclature, neutralization, reactions, ideal gas law, pH levels)
Understand general human anatomy and physiology related to occupational exposures
Identify and assess the sources, sampling, control strategies, symptoms, and target organs related to exposure hazards:
Physical (e.g., noise, ionizing radiation, non-ionizing radiation, heat/cold stress, vibration, light, respirable dust, nanoscale)
Chemical (e.g., asphyxiants, corrosives, reactive, irritants, sensitizers, carcinogens, mutagens, teratogens)
Biological (e.g., viral, bacterial, parasitic, fungus, mold)

Understand and differentiate among the types of occupational exposure limits (e.g., Short-Term Exposure Limits [STEL], Time-Weighted Average [TWA], Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health [IDLH], Ceiling)
Understand the routes of entry for hazardous substances
Understand and differentiate between acute and chronic exposures
Apply universal precautions for the control of pathogens (e.g., bloodborne, viral, bacterial)
Understand general ionizing radiation principles (e.g., decay, half-life, source strength, concentration, inverse square law)
Understand requirements for fitness for duty and return to work
Define key aspects of Total Worker Health®
Understand environmental hazards (e.g., biological, chemical, waste, radon)
Understand environmental impacts and best practices (e.g., spill/release, conservation), related to:
Water (e.g., drainage, waste)
Air (e.g., quality, carbon footprint)
Land (e.g., solid waste, recycling, soil)
Understand the hierarchy of conservation (e.g., reduce/reuse/recycle, waste energy)
Understand environmental management system standards for development of programs (e.g., ISO 14001)
Understand waste removal, treatment, classification, labeling, certification, and disposal
Understand the EHS role in environmental, social, and governance (ESG)
Apply appropriate learning theory and techniques
Use appropriate training tools (e.g., instructor-led, computer-based, group meeting, virtual)
Understand how to create a positive safety culture (e.g., open feedback, effective communication, psychological safety, emotional intelligence)
Facilitate data collection, needs analysis, gap analysis, and feedback
Define baseline competency to determine training needs
Assess training effectiveness and knowledge retention
Understand and identify human risk factors affecting performance (e.g., behavior, decision making, situation awareness, workload management, risk perception, stress)
Understand the requirements for and differences between competent and qualified persons
Understand compliance requirements and legal liability of safety professional practices (e.g., audits, sampling, reporting, procedural review)
Understand legal liability regarding contractor management and multi-employer worksites
Understand contract terminology and contract management lifecycle
Understand records control (e.g., retention, chain-of-custody, worker privacy)
Determine appropriate actions based on knowledge and scope limitations (e.g., cybersecurity, insurance, legal)
Understand the principles of risk transfer (e.g., outsourcing, insurance)
Understand liabilities relating to worker impairment (e.g., drugs, alcohol, fatigue, stress)
Describe the principles of minimizing hazards using Prevention-Through-Design (e.g., avoidance, elimination, substitution, safety design criteria for workplace facilities, machines, and practices)
Apply the principles of process safety (e.g., pressure relief systems, chemical compatibility, management of change, materials of construction, process flow diagrams)
Evaluate common workplace hazards (e.g., electrical, falls, confined spaces, lockout/tagout, working around water, caught in, struck by, excavation)
Evaluate facility life safety features (e.g., public space safety, floor loading, occupancy loads)

Describe fleet safety principles (e.g., driver and equipment safety, maintenance, surveillance equipment, GPS monitoring, telematics, hybrid vehicles, fuel systems, driving under the influence, fatigue)
Evaluate materials handling methods and controls (e.g., forklifts, aerial lifts, and other powered industrial trucks; cranes, hand trucks, hoists, rigging, manual handling, drones)
Evaluate the use of tools, machines, and equipment (e.g., hand tools, power tools, ladders, grinders, hydraulics, robotics)
Compare performance against established benchmarks (e.g., gap analysis)
Analyze performance standards to determine plan of action
Determine how to measure, analyze, and improve EHS culture
Determine appropriate incident investigation techniques (root causes) and apply corrective actions
Describe the Management of Change process (prior, during, after)
Describe system safety analysis techniques (e.g., fault tree analysis, failure modes and effects analysis [FMEA], Safety Case approach, risk summation)
Evaluate leading and lagging indicators
Recognize safety, health, and environmental management and audit systems (e.g., ISO 14000 series, 45001, 19011, ANSI Z10)
Describe required components for plans, systems, and policies (e.g., safety, health, and environmental regulations and standards)

Utilize document retention or management principles (e.g., incident investigation, training records, exposure records, maintenance records, environmental management system, audit results, privacy, trade secrets, personal information)
Apply budgeting, finance, and economic analysis techniques and principles (e.g., timelines, budget development, resourcing, return on investment, cost/benefit analysis, role in procurement process)
Differentiate management leadership techniques (e.g., management theories, leadership theories, motivation, discipline, authority, responsibility, accountability, communication styles)
Apply project management principles and techniques (e.g., RACI charts, project timelines)
Analyze and/or interpret data (e.g., exposure, release concentrations, sampling data, mean, median, mode, confidence intervals, probabilities, Pareto analysis)
Apply general principles of the safety risk evaluation process (i.e., identifying, analyzing, evaluating, monitoring, and communicating risk affecting an organization)
Apply risk management strategies to identify and mitigate EHS hazards (e.g., risk analysis, job hazard analysis, process hazard analysis, hierarchy of controls)
Differentiate financial risk mitigation strategies as they relate to risk avoidance, risk retention, risk sharing, risk transfer, loss prevention and reduction

Apply risk analysis process of identifying, ranking, and monitoring (e.g., disasters/emergency preparedness, fire prevention, occupational health, hazardous materials management/environmental compliance)
Create, employ, and maintain an Emergency Response Plan (e.g., fire, severe weather, nuclear incidents, natural disasters, terrorist attacks, chemical spills, utilities systems, cyber security)
Describe the elements in disaster response and recovery (e.g., incident command, business continuity, contingency plans)
Identify key components of fire prevention, protection, and suppression systems
Prepare procedures for the safe transportation and security of hazardous materials
Implement a workplace violence prevention program
Describe environmental protection and pollution prevention programs (e.g., spill containment, abatement, best practices)
Identify procedures used to manage hazardous materials (e.g., GHS classification system, storage and handling, policy, security, hazardous waste storage and disposal)
Identify procedures used to manage waste (e.g., universal, recycling, spill clean-up, labeling, remediation)
Determine sustainability principles and practices (e.g., supply chain; reduce, reuse, recycle)
Describe the impact of environmental issues (e.g., aging infrastructure, asbestos, air pollution, climate change, environmental, social, and governance)

Anticipate, recognize, evaluate, and control occupational exposures by implementing techniques for measurement, sampling, and analysis (e.g., hazardous chemicals, SDS, radiation, noise, biological hazards, heat/cold, indoor air quality, ventilation, nanoparticles, combustible dust, heat systems, high pressure, silica, powder and spray applications, blasting, molten metals, hot work, cold and heat stress, laser)
Understand principles of public health as applicable (i.e., fundamentals of epidemiology, infectious disease, risk factors, statistics to interpret data)

Apply toxicology principles to create exposure control plans and develop risk mitigation plans (e.g., using sampling equipment, symptoms of an exposure, LD50, LC50, mutagens, carcinogens, teratogens, ototoxins)
Evaluate principles related to ergonomics and human factors (e.g., visual acuity, body mechanics, lifting, vibration, anthropometrics, fatigue management)
Apply chemistry principles to calculate required containment volumes and hazardous materials storage requirements
Apply core concepts in physics (e.g., forms of energy, weights, forces, stresses)
Describe the needs assessment process to determine worker training, competencies, and qualifications
Develop training programs with training materials to address various learning styles (e.g., presentation methods and tools)
Describe how to implement training programs utilizing the Continuous Improvement model
Determine the effectiveness of training programs (e.g., surveys, on-the-job compliance, feedback, assessments, demonstrations, quizzes)
Demonstrate working knowledge of education and training methods and techniques (e.g., classroom, online, simulation, computer-based, Artificial Intelligence, coaching, on-the-job training)
Understand adult learning principles (e.g., visual, auditory, reading and writing, kinesthetic)
